claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Real direct CLI check this run — `claude --version` on the runner reports `2.1.270 (Claude Code)`, continuing the run of live-CLI validation since 2.1.257. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.268 to **2.1.270** together (no divergence), covering the 2.1.269 → 2.1.270 delta. 2.1.270 is a compatibility-only bump: it ships exactly one fix (read-only git commands in Bash unexpectedly re-asking for permission after a long-running session, a 2.1.269 regression) with no marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. Two items from 2.1.269 are directly relevant and documented: **`claude plugin eval`** — a new subcommand that runs a plugin's own eval suite against Claude Code and produces a scored, reproducible JSON+HTML report — noted in the install guide's Useful-flags section as the way a contributor (here, or in one of the three plugin repos this catalog points at) could smoke-test a listed plugin, though none of the three plugins in this catalog ship an eval suite of their own today; and **SECURITY: plugin archives extracted for a session could be readable by other local users, keep world-writable bits, or leave stale files surviving re-extraction** — documented in `docs/agent-guidelines/security.md` as a defense-in-depth note alongside the existing git-source-URL redaction rule, since this catalog's three manifests use only `github` sources (never `archive` sources), so no plugin installed from here was ever exposed, but the note stands for any future `archive`-source entry. Reviewed and not applicable, checked directly rather than assumed: a deny/ask permission rule starting with a bare `!` leaking beyond its settings source (2.1.269 fix) — this catalog documents no `Read()`/`Edit()`/permission-rule examples anywhere (checked via `grep`), matching the precedent set for the 2.1.259/2.1.260 permission-rule items; organization plugins via managed settings not loading in headless sessions (2.1.269 fix) — no managed-org marketplace or `enabledPlugins` configuration exists for this personal catalog, matching the existing 2.1.261 `@synced`-plugin note; plugin `headersHelper` consent prompts showing a misleading URL path (2.1.269 fix) — none of this catalog's three manifests use `headersHelper` today (checked via `grep`), so the display fix changes nothing here, though the install guide's existing `headersHelper` section covers the mechanism generally for a future private/token-gated entry; plugin errors showing `[redacted URL]` for Windows paths starting with `@` (2.1.269 fix) — this catalog ships no Windows-specific paths or scripts; the `Edit()`/write-path/`tee` permission-interaction fix (2.1.269) — no plugin source lives in this repo for that fix to touch; the attribution-reminder-overriding-CLAUDE.md fix (2.1.269) — this repo's own `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` attribution guidance was never affected since no managed-settings attribution override is configured here; and skills synced from claude.ai in cloud sessions now named `anthropic-skills:<name>` (2.1.269 change) — this catalog's own skill (`.agents/skills/run-plugins-catalog`) is a plain repo skill, not an Anthropic-authored skill and never cloud-synced, so the new naming convention doesn't apply to it, and neither `docs/agent-guidelines/style.md` nor the install guide claimed otherwise. `/ultrareview --post` posting a PR comment directly (2.1.269) and the other 2.1.269 Added items (`/output-style` over Remote Control, Bash file-change diff, the new OTEL/gateway/workflow-concurrency env vars, the `/focus` spinner tip) are host/session/CI-side with zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` (piped through `scripts/report-skill-validation.py`) and a full `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`, 3 plugins in sync, no drift) both passed clean against the live 2.1.270 CLI, confirmed again on a fresh clone of the final branch state.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
